data.overview: LOOKFANTASTIC is Europe's leading online premium beauty retailer, owned since 2010 by THG (The Hut Group). Available evidence is limited to a sustainability case study documenting a 72% cut in Beauty Box packaging emissions (produced by THG's own carbon partners), a company vegan-beauty category page, and an independent legitimacy review that flags fulfilment and after-sales complaints. No independent cruelty-free or vegan certification evidence for the brand appears in the fetched sources.

claims.claim: LOOKFANTASTIC states it demonstrated a proactive commitment to sustainability by reducing its Beauty Box packaging footprint through a Life Cycle Assessment.
claims.quote: LOOKFANTASTIC were able to demonstrate their proactive commitment to sustainability by conducting an LCA that helped reduce the environmental footprint of their Beauty Box packaging.

papers.title: LOOKFANTASTIC achieves a 72% reduction in Beauty Box packaging emissions
papers.summary: This case study, authored by LOOKFANTASTIC's own group sustainability arm THG Eco, reports that a redesign of the Beauty Box packaging cut overall packaging emissions by 72% while saving £2 million. The reductions were verified via a Life Cycle Assessment; remaining outer-packaging emissions were offset with carbon credits. As a company-affiliated source, the figures are self-reported.

findings.text: LOOKFANTASTIC reduced Beauty Box packaging emissions by 72% and saved £2 million in packaging and supply chain costs.
findings.quote: LOOKFANTASTIC reduced overall Beauty Box packaging emissions by 72%, offset the remaining emissions for its outer packaging and saved £2 million across packaging and supply chain costs as a result.

findings.text: The packaging redesign cut packaging weight by 61%, reducing fuel usage in distribution.
findings.quote: 61% reduction in BB packaging weight – resulting in reduced overall fuel usage

findings.text: LOOKFANTASTIC is part of THG Holdings plc, a global ecommerce group and brand owner.
findings.quote: LOOKFANTASTIC forms part of THG Holdings plc, a leading global ecommerce group and brand owner.

papers.title: Sustainable Packaging Saving LOOKFANTASTIC £2 Million
papers.summary: MyCarbon, described as THG's sustainability partner since 2021, conducted a Life Cycle Assessment of LOOKFANTASTIC's Beauty Box packaging. It reports the redesign cut cardboard use by 61.4% and total carbon footprint by 72.48%, partly by moving shipping from China to the EU. As THG's contracted partner, the source is company-affiliated rather than independent.

findings.text: The packaging upgrade was projected to decrease cardboard used by 61.4% and total footprint by roughly 72%.
findings.quote: the packaging upgrade would decrease the paper/ cardboard used by 61.4%. Moving the shipping location to the EU, and embracing a minimalist style with reduce the total carbon footprint by 72.48%

findings.text: Production in China and reliance on sea freight were identified as major contributors to LOOKFANTASTIC's emissions.
findings.quote: production in China and reliance on sea freight were major contributors to Look Fantastic’s emissions.

papers.title: Lookfantastic Review 2026: Is Lookfantastic Legit & Safe?
papers.fundingDisclosure: The source states it is independent and non-commercial, with no affiliate links, commissions, sponsorships or ads.
papers.summary: Atop Legal, a self-described independent non-commercial reviewer, rates Lookfantastic 70/100 (Grade B). It confirms the retailer is legitimate and THG-owned, selling genuine products with fast worldwide shipping, but flags recurring complaints about missing items, a 30-day return stance applied even to faulty goods, difficult customer service, and beauty-box subscriptions that auto-renew without clear consent.

findings.text: Lookfantastic is a legitimate THG-owned retailer, not a scam, carrying genuine products.
findings.quote: Lookfantastic is a legitimate online beauty retailer — founded in the UK in 1996 and owned since 2010 by THG (The Hut Group) — not a scam.

findings.text: Recurring complaints involve missing items, returns handling, customer service, and auto-renewing subscriptions.
findings.quote: missing items from larger orders (sometimes with hard-to-recover refunds), a 30-day return stance applied even to faulty goods, exhausting customer service, and beauty-box subscriptions that can auto-renew without clear consent.
